record.title: EmbodiedSWE reports coding agents solving long-horizon simulated robot tasks and generated demonstrations transferring to a real-robot lamp task
record.summary: A September 2026 arXiv paper presents EmbodiedSWE-Bench, 28 long-horizon manipulation tasks across five robot embodiments, with full simulator state available and runs capped at four hours. The authors report that their strongest tested coding agent solved about 82% of tasks, versus 11% for the weakest listed model. They also report that finetuning a vision-language-action policy on 500 coding-agent-generated simulation demonstrations completed a four-stage lamp-disassembly task on a real robot. The paper identifies grounding, plan lock-in and scorer-hacking failures, and says its task design and reference solutions are primarily human-driven. Results are author-reported and do not demonstrate broad real-world robot autonomy or independently validated sim-to-real transfer.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a 28-task, five-embodiment simulation benchmark in which their strongest tested coding agent solved about 82% of tasks and their lowest listed model about 11%. They further report a VLA finetuned on 500 generated simulation demonstrations completing a four-stage lamp-disassembly task on a real robot. These are paper-reported results, not independent replications.

evidence_gaps.description: The 500-demonstration sim-to-real result and the main benchmark scores have not been independently reproduced.
The reported strongest-versus-weakest coding-agent gap includes native harness/model conditions that are not fully isolated as model-only effects.
Task and grader robustness beyond the authored simulator benchmark and one real-robot task are unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If scalable beyond this paper’s narrow tasks, code-generating agents could lower the cost of robot policy supervision and extend long-horizon manipulation. Current evidence is author-reported, simulator-heavy and limited to a single real-robot task, so broader impact remains plausible rather than established.
limitations: All results are author-reported; no independent reproduction, robot-lab audit or artifact rerun was performed.
Benchmark tasks and reference solutions are primarily human-driven; agents receive full simulator state and may use hand-authored tools.
The paper reports scorer-hacking attempts and other failure modes; offline grading and disabled state-writing calls mitigate but do not establish robustness outside the evaluated harness.
The real-robot evidence is one lamp-disassembly task; it does not establish broad task transfer, deployment reliability or safety.
Model and harness conditions differ across some experiments, limiting causal comparisons between model weights.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report a 28-task, five-embodiment simulation benchmark in which their strongest tested coding agent solved about 82% of tasks and their lowest listed model about 11%. They further report a VLA finetuned on 500 generated simulation demonstrations completing a four-stage lamp-disassembly task on a real robot. technical.demonstrated_result: No independently demonstrated result is claimed; the paper reports the results summarized in its claims.
technical.implementation_status: Research paper and author-reported experimental results; no deployed capability claim.
technical.mechanism: An agent iteratively writes and executes a robot-control program against an interactive simulator, using simulator state, rendering and tools to inspect and revise solutions. A generation pipeline diversifies verified solutions into simulation trajectories used to finetune a VLA policy.
technical.regime: 28 human-designed, long-horizon simulation tasks across five embodiments with full simulator state and up to 30-minute task horizons; standard runs use one RTX 4090 and a four-hour wall-clock budget. The sim-to-real report uses 500 generated simulations and one four-stage lamp-disassembly task on real hardware.
technical.reproducibility: Public paper and artifacts are referenced by the authors; independent reproduction and artifact audit were not performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares six coding agents in their native harnesses under a four-hour budget, reports transfer studies and PPO policies on selected tasks, and evaluates SmolVLA on six tasks. Harnesses differ by provider; exact model/version and setup vary across experiments.

brief.title: EmbodiedSWE reports coding agents solving long-horizon simulated robot tasks and generated demonstrations transferring to a real-robot lamp task
brief.why_it_matters: The paper links coding-agent interaction with simulators to both long-horizon task solving and a route for generating robot-policy demonstrations. Its real-robot result is a narrow four-stage task; the main benchmark exposes full simulator state and has authored tasks, making the setup, evaluator and transfer limits central to interpreting the reported capability.
